personas.background: Trail running coach, the de facto group leader. Pushes the group toward harder routes than some members want. Competitive, energetic, genuinely doesn't understand why anyone would want to take the easy trail.

food.value: obsessive about post-hike protein — always suggests the same spot for a protein bowl after every hike

activities.value: strongly prefers steep, technical trails over flat routes; gets visibly restless on easy hikes

preference_history.old_value: would compromise on easier routes for the group
preference_history.new_value: consistently pushes for harder trails and dismisses concerns about difficulty
preference_history.trigger: started training for an ultramarathon; her tolerance for easy routes dropped

speaking_quirks: names every trail by its technical designation
refers to easy trails as 'the tourist path'

personas.background: Accountant. Joined the group 3 years ago. Genuinely enjoys hiking but is starting to struggle with the pace Dani sets. Has a knee that flares up on descents but doesn't want to admit it.

food.value: always brings his own packed lunch; never wants to stop at a cafe after a hike

activities.value: prefers moderate trails — secretly struggling with the group's increasing pace and difficulty

preference_history.old_value: could manage any descent without issue
preference_history.new_value: knee flares up on steep descents; avoids saying this directly, volunteers for route-finding duties instead
preference_history.trigger: knee injury from a scramble in session 3

speaking_quirks: uses weather as a proxy for trail difficulty — 'should be fine' means he's nervous
volunteers to carry the map/navigation duty to avoid leading on technical sections
sends practical logistics without opinion: 'parking is at the layby on the B4086'

personas.background: NHS physio who joined to stay active and socialize. Competent hiker but here primarily for the social element. The one who suggests the cafe stops Dani resists. Has strong opinions about proper warm-ups that no one else cares about.

food.value: always wants to stop for tea and cake mid-hike or after — the social ritual matters as much as the walk

activities.value: prefers moderate trails with good views and conversation time; dislikes routes where everyone is too winded to talk

preference_history.old_value: kept up with group pace without comment
preference_history.new_value: started explicitly pushing back on 'no stops' policies after session 2
preference_history.trigger: felt the group was becoming a training exercise rather than a social walk

speaking_quirks: always mentions the cafe she wants to stop at by name
brings up 'the social side' when Dani proposes no-stop routes
sends photos of views mid-hike to the chat

personas.background: Secondary school teacher, the quietest in the group. Solid hiker but can't do weekends after September due to marking season. Everyone forgets this every year. Also mildly allergic to wasps, which becomes relevant.

food.value: carries an EpiPen due to wasp allergy; always checks outdoor seating plans before confirming a cafe stop

activities.value: unavailable for weekend hikes September onwards due to marking and teaching load

preference_history.new_value: explicitly unavailable September-November due to teaching; the group keeps forgetting
preference_history.trigger: confirmed unavailability for autumn schedule in session 4 — has said this before but group ignores it

speaking_quirks: replies to Dani's trail suggestions with one-word assessments: 'manageable', 'steep', 'doable'

personas.background: PhD student in ecology, newest member. Joined six months ago. Loves being outdoors but hates the competitive element that Dani brings. Often conflated with Bev by newer group correspondents because they're both enthusiastic and both push back on hard routes, but for different reasons — Bev is social, Cass is environment-focused.

food.value: vegan; always checks that cafe stops have something plant-based, doesn't make a fuss about it

activities.value: prefers routes that go through woodland or wildlife-rich areas rather than open ridgelines

preference_history.old_value: happy with any route the group chose
preference_history.new_value: starting to advocate for lowland/woodland routes after learning they've been disturbing ground-nesting birds on ridge routes
preference_history.trigger: discovered their regular ridgeline disturbs ground-nesting birds during season; became vocal about it from session 3

speaking_quirks: references ecology and wildlife in trail discussions where others reference elevation gain
pushes back on ridge routes by citing bird disturbance rather than difficulty
uses 'actually' a lot when correcting something

edges.history_summary: Started the group together three years ago. Dani sets the pace; Marcus quietly keeps up.
Dani wants harder routes; Bev wants cafe stops. They negotiate constantly.
shared_events: argument about whether to stop at the Heron Cafe last August

edges.history_summary: Yusuf quietly matches Dani's pace and rarely complains, which she respects.
Dani likes Cass's fitness but is irritated by the ecology detours.
Both prefer moderate routes and have become quiet allies against Dani's escalating ambitions.
shared_events: both stayed behind when Dani and Yusuf went for the summit scramble

edges.history_summary: Comfortable hiking companions who don't socialize outside the group much.
Marcus appreciates Cass's steadiness and they've had good conversations on flatter sections.
Bev and Yusuf both appreciate the social side of hiking; they often end up chatting at the back.
Both push back on Dani's hardest routes, which makes people confuse their reasoning.
shared_events: both suggested stopping at the woodland path rather than the ridgeline on the same hike

edges.history_summary: Least interaction in the group; pleasant but not close.

group_norms.norm_text: No stopping mid-hike unless it's an emergency — we stop at the summit or the end.
Everyone picks their own route difficulty from the options Dani provides.
September and October are peak season — we do bigger routes then.
